issue.title: Revisit target provider implementations

repository.name: prometheus
repository.description: The Prometheus monitoring system and time series database.

issue.body:
Various SD integrations are not using the given channels correctly. Most commonly they send on the update channel without listening on the done channel to abort in case the consumer is gone. This can cause deadlocking of single goroutines or the entire server.

Generally, the pattern of starting background processing before `Run()` is called should be reconsidered as well.

My suspicion is that the cause has something to do with AWS itself: earlier today, I had issues with Prometheus, where it was repeatedly crashing due to [a panic](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/3001) in its EC2 service discovery mechanism, specifically in the code that handles Tags. I'm also experiencing issues when running Terraform due to what appears to be [malformed responses](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/issues/1628) given by the EC2 API to the golang client. In any case, I already opened a Case there to see what's going on there.

After manually restarting the controller-manager I could see these events:

```
  2m            2m              1       service-controller                      Normal          CreatingLoadBalancer            Creating load balancer
  2m            2m              1       service-controller                      Normal          CreatedLoadBalancer             Created load balancer
```

This gave me the chills since I thought Kubernetes created a whole new ELB for my production service, but after checking the `LoadBalancer Ingress` name, I could verify it successfully reused the correct ELB.

After doing that, all instances were registered to all ELBs.

**What you expected to happen**:

I could never expect that Kubernetes would de-register _all_ worker nodes from _all_ Service-managed ELBs, even in my wildest dreams (or nightmares), even in cases where the EC2 API were unstable, unresponsive or otherwise misbehaving in some way.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

I'm not sure how this could be reproduced.
